07

SQL Data Cleaning & Quality Project

SQL Server • T-SQL • Data Quality • Practice Project

A portfolio practice project that demonstrates how I would clean and prepare a raw sales table before analysis. The workflow focuses on data-quality checks, standardization, duplicate handling, validation rules, and producing a clean analytical table ready for reporting.

  • Detect duplicate transactions using GROUP BY and ROW_NUMBER()
  • Standardize text values with TRIM-style cleaning
  • Identify NULL, blank, negative, and invalid records
  • Create a clean reporting table with calculated gross sales
  • Build a final data-quality summary for validation
SQL Server T-SQL CTE ROW_NUMBER Data Cleaning Data Validation
SQL Data Cleaning WorkflowPractice Project
-- SQL Data Cleaning & Quality Project
-- Sample project for portfolio demonstration

-- 1) Find duplicate records
SELECT
    customer_id,
    transaction_date,
    product_id,
    COUNT(*) AS duplicate_count
FROM sales_raw
GROUP BY customer_id, transaction_date, product_id
HAVING COUNT(*) > 1;

-- 2) Standardize text fields
UPDATE sales_raw
SET
    customer_name = LTRIM(RTRIM(customer_name)),
    city = UPPER(LTRIM(RTRIM(city))),
    channel = LTRIM(RTRIM(channel));

-- 3) Detect missing / invalid values
SELECT *
FROM sales_raw
WHERE customer_id IS NULL
   OR product_id IS NULL
   OR quantity IS NULL
   OR quantity < 0
   OR unit_price < 0;

-- 4) Replace blank text with NULL
UPDATE sales_raw
SET city = NULL
WHERE LTRIM(RTRIM(city)) = '';

-- 5) Remove exact duplicates using ROW_NUMBER
WITH DuplicateRows AS (
    SELECT *,
           ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
               PARTITION BY customer_id, transaction_date, product_id, quantity, unit_price
               ORDER BY transaction_id
           ) AS rn
    FROM sales_raw
)
DELETE FROM DuplicateRows
WHERE rn > 1;

-- 6) Create a clean analytical table
SELECT
    transaction_id,
    customer_id,
    product_id,
    CAST(transaction_date AS date) AS transaction_date,
    quantity,
    unit_price,
    quantity * unit_price AS gross_sales,
    NULLIF(LTRIM(RTRIM(city)), '') AS city,
    NULLIF(LTRIM(RTRIM(channel)), '') AS channel
INTO sales_clean
FROM sales_raw
WHERE quantity >= 0
  AND unit_price >= 0
  AND customer_id IS NOT NULL
  AND product_id IS NOT NULL;

-- 7) Data quality summary
SELECT
    COUNT(*) AS total_rows,
    COUNT(DISTINCT customer_id) AS unique_customers,
    COUNT(DISTINCT product_id) AS unique_products,
    SUM(CASE WHEN city IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS missing_city_rows
FROM sales_clean;
